newsitem.title: CHINA: China parliament sets up new committee for HK.
newsitem.headline: China parliament sets up new committee for HK.

text.p: China's parliament moved on Friday to stamp its seal on Beijing's takeover of Hong Kong, setting up a special committee to monitor the territory's mini-constitution.

The standing committee of the National People's Congress opened a week-long session clearly timed to coincide with the return of the British colony to Chinese rule and to ensure Beijing could complete legal formalities linked to the handover.
It approved the 12-member Committee for the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, with six members from Hong Kong and the rest from China, the official Xinhua news agency said.

The newest body in a series of organisations China has established to handle Hong Kong affairs was due to start its work on July 1 -- the day China recovers the enclave after 156 years of British colonial rule.

Tying up legal loose ends, the parliament also decided that 10 national-level laws should be enforced in Hong Kong after the handover at midnight next Monday -- including the national flag law and a law on territorial waters.

The most timely item of legislation was the Garrison Law of People's Liberation Army troops stationed in the enclave, placed before parliament just as Beijing announced it would send 4,000 soldiers into Hong Kong just six hours after resuming sovereignty.

China's parliament committee began deliberation on scrapping the Hong Kong Preparatory Committee, a Beijing-selected body created to pave the way for the change of sovereignty. The final plenum of the committee is due on July 11, when it will announce its demise.

The stream of legislation was essential to ensure no legal loopholes when Beijing recovers sovereignty and replaces Hong Kong's partly-elected legislative council with a hand-picked provisional assembly on July 1, diplomats said.
The Garrison Law was necessary to ensure Beijing could administer Hong Kong's defence from its resumption of sovereignty at midnight (1600 GMT) on Monday, Xinhua said.

A total of 509 troops will arrive shortly before the handover ceremony. The next wave of 4,000 will arrive just after dawn, accompanied by 10 ships, six helicopters, 21 armoured cars and 400 other vehicles.
The troops will enter shortly after the popularly-elected legislature is dissolved.
Chinese naval vessels will churn through waters crossed a few hours earlier by the British royal yacht Britannia, carrying Patten and heir-to-the-throne Prince Charles home to Britain.
China trumpeted the decision on its evening nationwide television news, saying the soldiers would enter through three border posts, depicted in detail on a topographical chart.
The new special committee will have responsibility for "making suggestions and offering ideas" for revision and amendment of Hong Kong's Basic Law -- its mini-constitution, Xinhua said.
China's parliament must consult the committee before giving interpretations of the Basic Law, Xinhua said.
Hong Kong will have its own legislature, the Beijing-appointed Provisional Legislative Council that has pledged to hold elections within a year under rules still to be agreed.
